summary: Specifies the non-media data transport aspects of WebRTC, giving an architectural overview of how SCTP is used as a generic transport service so browsers can exchange non-media data directly.

eli5.summary: Besides video, browsers can pass files and messages straight to each other. This explains the pipe they use.

questions: how do webrtc data channels work
why does webrtc use sctp over dtls
what is the maximum webrtc data channel message size
subtitle: How browsers send arbitrary non-media data to each other: SCTP carried over DTLS over ICE/UDP.

tldr.problem: WebRTC lets two browsers exchange audio and video, but applications such as games, file transfer and text chat also need to send non-media data directly between peers, securely, through NATs and with congestion control.
tldr.mechanism: Data channels run over SCTP, which is encapsulated in DTLS over ICE/UDP. A data channel is a pair of SCTP streams (one in each direction) with the same stream identifier, with per-message choices of reliable or partially reliable and ordered or unordered delivery.
tldr.outcome: Browsers get WebSocket-like bidirectional channels that can share a single UDP port with the media, with confidentiality, source authentication and integrity, and NAT traversal.

facts.label: Initial IP-layer path MTU
facts.value: SHOULD NOT exceed 1200 bytes (IPv4) or 1280 bytes (IPv6)

today: RFC 8831 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The in-band opening protocol it relies on is specified in RFC 8832.

sections.title: Non-Media Data in WebRTC
sections.content:
WebRTC communication consists of media (audio and video) and non-media data. Media travels over SRTP and is not covered here. Non-media data uses the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP, RFC 4960) encapsulated in DTLS.

The stack is SCTP on top of DTLS on top of ICE/UDP. Encapsulating SCTP over DTLS (RFC 8261) over ICE/UDP (RFC 8445) gives a NAT traversal solution plus confidentiality, source authentication and integrity-protected transfers. This service runs in parallel with the SRTP media transports, and all of them can eventually share a single UDP port number.

SCTP brings several streams, and both reliable and partially reliable delivery for user messages. The RFC adds extensions: stream reconfiguration (RFC 6525) to add streams and reset individual ones, and RFC 8260 to interleave large messages and prioritize streams.
sections.eli5: Videos already have a tube between browsers. This builds a second, lockable tube for everything else, such as files and chat.

sections.title: Use Cases and Requirements
sections.content:
The informational use cases split into unreliable and reliable channels. Unreliable examples are position updates in a real-time game and non-critical status such as mute state in a video chat. Reliable examples are critical game state, file transfers between people chatting, text chat during a call, renegotiating the PeerConnection and proxy browsing over HTTP/HTTPS.

The ten requirements include multiple simultaneous channels, both reliable and unreliable modes, congestion control, application-supplied priorities, security, and message fragmentation so that large messages do not need IP-layer fragmentation or delay other channels. The protocol must not put local IP addresses in its fields, must support Path MTU discovery without relying on ICMP, and must be implementable in user application space.
sections.eli5: Some messages must arrive perfectly, like a file. Others, like a player's position, are stale a moment later, so a lost one does not matter. The tube has to handle both.

sections.title: SCTP over DTLS over UDP
sections.content:
SCTP is chosen for features that match the requirements: TCP-friendly congestion control that can be modified to cooperate with media congestion control, multiple unidirectional streams, ordered and out-of-order delivery, fragmentation and reassembly of arbitrarily large messages, PMTU discovery, and reliable or partially reliable transport. Multihoming is not supported: SCTP acts as if running on a single-homed host.

Each SCTP user message carries a Payload Protocol Identifier (PPID). In WebRTC it distinguishes UTF-8 text, binary data and the Data Channel Establishment Protocol (RFC 8832). The PPID is not exposed to the JavaScript API.

The RFC chose this stack over DTLS over SCTP (RFC 6083) combined with SCTP over UDP (RFC 6951) because it supports arbitrarily large user messages, shares the DTLS connection with the SRTP media, and keeps SCTP control information private.

Practical rules follow from running over UDP. SCTP MUST do Path MTU discovery without ICMP or ICMPv6, using probing as in RFC 4821 and RFC 4820, and the initial path MTU at the IP layer SHOULD NOT exceed 1200 bytes for IPv4 and 1280 bytes for IPv6. SCTP SHOULD be notified of an address change and in that case should retest the path MTU and reset congestion state to its initial state. All SCTP streams in an association share one congestion window.

Required SCTP extensions are: stream reconfiguration (RFC 6525, used for closing channels), dynamic address reconfiguration (RFC 5061, only to signal support for stream reset), partial reliability (RFC 3758) and the limited retransmission policy (RFC 7496). Zero retransmissions with unordered delivery gives a UDP-like service. Message interleaving (RFC 8260) SHOULD be used.
sections.eli5: The tube is built from layers: a careful delivery service on top, a lock in the middle, and a postal van at the bottom that can get past home routers.

sections.title: What a Data Channel Is
sections.content:
An SCTP stream is a unidirectional logical channel inside an association. Ordering is preserved only for ordered messages on the same stream.

A data channel is a pair of one incoming and one outgoing SCTP stream with the same stream identifier, so it is bidirectional. This lets the API closely mirror WebSockets. Each channel has, in each direction, a reliable or unreliable mode, in-order or out-of-order delivery, a priority, an optional label and an optional protocol. Reliability and ordering are in fact properties of SCTP user messages rather than streams.

Priority is a 2-byte unsigned integer interpreted as a weighted-fair-queuing priority per RFC 8260. For WebRTC the values SHOULD be one of 128 (below normal), 256 (normal), 512 (high) or 1024 (extra high).
sections.eli5: One lane carries things one way and another carries things back. Put them side by side and you have a two-way road that can also be marked as a fast lane.

sections.title: Association, Opening and Closing
sections.content:
The SCTP association is set up when the two endpoints agree to open it, as negotiated by JSEP, typically an SDP exchange. It uses the DTLS connection selected by ICE, typically shared via BUNDLE with the DTLS connections that key the SRTP media. The number of streams negotiated SHOULD be 65535, the maximum. If the association closes, gracefully or not, all its data channels close; after a non-graceful teardown an error indication SHOULD be provided if possible.

Channels are opened either by in-band negotiation (a simple protocol is given in RFC 8832) or out-of-band, in a way the RFC leaves out of scope. With out-of-band opening, unless otherwise negotiated, the client picks even stream identifiers and the server picks odd ones, according to the DTLS role. The application must avoid collisions: reusing a stream that belongs to an existing channel MUST fail.

To close a channel, one side resets its outgoing stream (RFC 6525). When the peer sees the incoming stream reset, it resets its own outgoing stream, and then the channel is closed. The reset returns the stream sequence numbers to zero, the stream can be reused, and all messages are delivered or abandoned before the reset.
sections.eli5: To hang up a lane, you shut your end, your friend sees it shut and shuts theirs, and then the lane can be used again.

sections.title: Sending Messages
sections.content:
Data on a channel is sent over its stream with the reliability chosen when the channel was opened, unless options change or per-message options are given. Because SCTP preserves message boundaries, a sender MUST put exactly one application message in each SCTP user message (unless the deprecated PPID-based fragmentation is used).

The PPID signals what the payload is: WebRTC String for a non-empty UTF-8 string, WebRTC Binary for non-empty binary data, and WebRTC String Empty or WebRTC Binary Empty for empty messages. SCTP cannot send empty user messages, so an empty message is sent as one zero byte with the matching PPID, and the receiver ignores that byte and treats the message as empty. The Partial PPIDs are deprecated. A receiver that gets an unsupported PPID or detects an error such as illegal ordering SHOULD close the channel.

Without message interleaving, a big message can monopolize the association, so the sender SHOULD limit messages to 16 KB. The maximum message size has to be negotiated, for example via RFC 8841. The sender SHOULD disable the Nagle algorithm to minimize latency.
sections.eli5: Each note goes in its own envelope, with a sticker saying whether it is text or a file. An empty note still gets an envelope, with a special sticker.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: This document adds no security considerations beyond those in RFC 8826 and RFC 8827. The one extra note is that a receiver must be prepared for a sender that tries to send arbitrarily large messages. DTLS protects the complete SCTP packet, so the stack provides confidentiality, integrity and source authentication for it.
sections.eli5: The tube is locked, so outsiders cannot read or change what goes through. A receiver should still be ready for someone sending a giant package.

sections.title: Registered Payload Protocol Identifiers
sections.content: The RFC uses six SCTP Payload Protocol Identifiers that were already registered. IANA updated their reference to this document and renamed the first four, leaving the dates unchanged. The values are 51 (WebRTC String), 52 (WebRTC Binary Partial, deprecated), 53 (WebRTC Binary), 54 (WebRTC String Partial, deprecated), 56 (WebRTC String Empty) and 57 (WebRTC Binary Empty).
sections.eli5: The stickers used on the envelopes already had official numbers. They were just renamed and pointed at this document.
